_meta.source: MLB_GPP_Master_Playbook_v4.md, Section 10 (Standing Rules Ledger) + Section 11 (Ledger Governance)
_meta.rule_type_note: rule_type is a DRAFT first-pass tag (coverage / allocation / gate) per the coverage-vs-allocation framework in DFS_Sim-Overlay_Operating_Model_PORTABLE.md. Coverage rules force a winning configuration to exist and should be applied freely. Allocation rules bet on how much of something and are presumed harmful when a sim baseline is in use. Gate rules are hard build-time constraints (pass/fail). Have Shaun review/correct these tags before wiring them into the governance dashboard's allocation-override warnings.
_meta.active_flag_note: active=false rows are folded/superseded per the v4 consolidation pass; folded_into points to the surviving rule. Keep folded rows in the table (greyed in UI) rather than deleting them, per the Playbook's explicit numbering-not-resequenced convention.

rules.text: xSLG pitcher cap — SP facing opp xSLG > 0.45 capped at 15%.
rules.rationale: Elder -6.5 in 45% (5/27); gate deleted Cavalli/Wrobleski/Liberatore (6/30).

rules.text: Salary floor $48,500 across all lineups.
Never zero any team. Environment filters are WEIGHTING tools, not exclusion filters.
rules.rationale: BAL/BOS/HOU zeroed 5/27 finished top-3.

rules.text: Evergreen principles over team-specific fixes.
Hash-based deduplication before submission.
DK position sourcing from the entries file — parse COMBINED eligibility ('1B/OF') correctly.
rules.rationale: Position errors (5/27); multi-pos parser bug dropped Ohtani/Edman/Stowers (6/30).

rules.text: Ownership-balance flag — heavy single-player exposure triggers a field comparison.
Find the underowned premium arm with ceiling every slate. Reconcile with #1 via #31.
The dart — a confirmed cheap bat moving up the order.
Coors + park/weather as first-class inputs. Extended by #35/#36; qualified by #47.
Delay ≠ Postponement. Cap weather-risk at ~15%, monitor for official postponement only. NOW QUALIFIED BY #48: applies to FORECAST risk only.
rules.rationale: Foster Griffin delayed-not-postponed was slate-best (6/22).

rules.text: Never anchor the slate's most-owned SP; confirm field own below 30% before >20 LUs. Refined by #37/#38.
Single-player hitter exposure cap: 50%. Unenforceable below ~6 lineups (granularity floor).
rules.rationale: Caminero 77% (6/22); n=3 portfolio forced 67% exposures (7/27).

rules.text: On a short slate, correlate through the SP's own GAME. Diversify two-SP builds across games.
rules.rationale: Both SPs' offenses bust = every lineup fails (6/22).

rules.text: Never zero any team's BATTING stack — anti-corr bans hitters FACING the SP, not teammate bats. Every team's bats in ≥5-10 LUs.
rules.rationale: KC Caglianone/Loftin 6-7% owned, zero exposure (6/23).

rules.text: For every SP with major anti-corr impact, build a defined allocation WITHOUT that SP.
rules.rationale: ~170 FPTS of blocked bats (6/23).

rules.text: ROO ceiling is a weighting input, not an environment guarantee. Allocate across ≥4 of 5 environments.
rules.rationale: Top pre-slate environment busted 4 straight (TB/STL/SEA/MIN).

rules.text: The dart-pitcher rule: 1-2 Chase LUs on the lowest-owned viable SP from the right game.
rules.rationale: Avila 2.1%/20.45 excluded as Tier-4 (6/23).

rules.text: On a 5-game turbo, prefer 2-3-man partial stacks; full 5-mans are for 8+ game slates.
rules.rationale: PHI 5-man 3-of-5 bust (6/23).

rules.text: Split same-tier same-team stack anchors rather than rostering both everywhere.
rules.rationale: J-Rod + Arozarena both 0 in 17 LUs each (6/23).

rules.text: Stack ownership cap — target ≥3 of 5 primary bats sub-10% INDIVIDUAL own. Qualified by #32.
rules.rationale: Large-field winners averaged single-digit stack own (Winner Study).

rules.text: Mandate one sub-4%-owned top-6 ceiling bat per lineup. Recompute the dart pool AFTER the #42 transform in sharp fields.
rules.rationale: A sub-4% 30+ bat won all 8 studied slates (Winner Study); T. White 2.1%→6.3% post-transform (7/27).

rules.text: Build ≥1 full 5-stack of the cheapest viable home offense in a hitter's park.
rules.rationale: 220-234-pt ceilings from cheap teams (Winner Study); Coors 6/30, 7/3.

rules.text: Pitcher pairing = 1 anchor + 1 sub-15% K arm. Do not pair two 35%+ chalk SPs. Qualified by #33/#34/#39.
rules.rationale: Two-35%+ pairs in 0% of winners (Winner Study) — EXCEPT thin-arm slates (#39).

rules.text: Primary + 2-3-man secondary mini from a different game.
rules.rationale: Secondary mini in 46-77% of top-100 (Winner Study); 57-72% again 6/30-7/5.

rules.text: Stop optimizing to avoid zeros; audit for stack QUALITY (ceiling), not floor. VOID below ~1,000 entries per #44.
rules.rationale: Winners ate 1-3.6 dead bats (Winner Study); 7/5 winner won with a 0-FPTS bat.

rules.text: Match stack size to slate scoring, not habit.
rules.rationale: 5-stack share 1%→86% by slate (Winner Study).

rules.text: Singular-leverage-arm concentration — top-projection AND lowest-owned arm: do not trim below ~40% for diversification alone.
rules.rationale: Mize top proj + 6.9% own; trimmed to 34.7% (6/29).

rules.text: Aggregate stack ownership ≠ concentrated chalk. Check INDIVIDUAL bat ownership before fading a strong offense. (Absorbs #32: weight primary stacks by individual-bat ownership; if ≥3 bats are sub-10% owned, the stack is LIVE regardless of team total.)
rules.rationale: LAD 33% aggregate faded to 7.3%, bats 5-8%, co-winning stack (6/29). MIA ~90% team-owned but bats 4-11%, winning stack + 54% of top-1% (6/30). Inverse confirmed: BOS 130.4% aggregate with ZERO sub-10% bats = true trap, 0.48x lift (7/27).

rules.text: Build the dart INTO the stack — force the cheapest sub-4% bat in that team's order into a defined share.
rules.rationale: Missed Cole Young 1.4%/33, Conine 0% (6/29).

rules.text: xSLG gate is a HR-risk FLAG, not a hard exclusion of low-owned arms. A capped arm ALSO sub-6% owned is a leverage arm — build a defined Chase block (10-20%). Reconciles #1 with #8.
rules.rationale: Cavalli 45.1/2.6%, Wrobleski 31.6/3.8%, Liberatore 27.6/1.2% capped to 0 (6/30).

rules.text: Weight primary stacks by INDIVIDUAL-bat ownership, never team-aggregate. If ≥3 bats are sub-10% owned, the stack is LIVE regardless of team total. (Hard version of #29.)
rules.rationale: MIA ~90% team-owned but bats 4-11%; winning stack + 54% of top-1% (6/30). Inverse confirmed: BOS 130.4% aggregate with ZERO sub-10% bats = true trap, 0.48x lift (7/27).

rules.text: Do not floor two premium anchors to the same high share. Cap any single SP at ~20% AND require the second-arm pool to include the chalk aces the field is correctly riding.
rules.rationale: Schlittler+Joe Ryan floored 20% each = 60 LUs; both busted (6/30).

rules.text: Detect the chalk-live slate. Build a defined chalk-anchored block (25-30%). Max-leverage is a bet the field is wrong — size it, do not force it.
rules.rationale: Top-1% avg own 10.2%; MIA+CHC 85% of top-1% stacks (6/30).

rules.text: Coors series persistence. A Coors game is a first-class primary environment EVERY day of the series. Build 5-mans of BOTH sides for the series duration.
rules.rationale: MIA 253.45 (6/30); COL 244.25 (7/3), alternating sides of one series.

rules.text: Bad-team Coors bats stay underowned all series. Expect 1-11% individual ownership to persist even after a blowup.
rules.rationale: MIA bats 4-11% (6/30); COL bats 0.7-7% (7/3) after a 14-run game.

rules.text: Hero-chalk fade (the Cavalli rule). When a leverage SP posts a viral score and next-start projected ownership jumps ≥5x baseline, hard-fade: cap at ≤5% and treat the fade as the leverage position.
rules.rationale: Cavalli 2.6%/45.15 → 38.3%/0.45. Zero top-100 rostered him (7/5).

rules.text: Chalk-SP classification: NARRATIVE vs STRUCTURAL. Narrative (hype/highlight/cheap price) → fade hard per #12/#37. Structural (only viable arms on a thin-SP slate) → see #39.
rules.rationale: Imai and Cavalli (narrative) 0% of top-100; Miller/Eovaldi (structural) 93%/78% of top-100.

rules.text: Thin-arm slate exception. When two SPs are clearly best on a weak slate (both 35%+ projected), roster BOTH and generate ALL differentiation through sub-10% bats.
rules.rationale: 7/2: 73% of top-100 ran Miller+Eovaldi; winner had 8 bats under 10% (avg 7.2%).

rules.text: IL-return star scan. Check confirmed lineups for top bats in their first 1-3 games back. A star under ~3% projected own is an automatic #22 dart at superstar ceiling.
rules.rationale: Yordan Alvarez 1.96%/39 in the 7/4 winner, Altuve 1.48%/23 beside him.

rules.text: SP-own-offense mandate. When any SP is rostered at structural-chalk conviction (35%+ projected, or structural under #38), a build pairing him with his own offense MUST enter the tested candidate set. BROADENED 7/27: applies to ANY gate-passing arm whose offense clears the stack screen, at any ownership.
rules.rationale: 7/26 winner ran Miso + Vaughn/Chourio. 7/27 winner ran Thornton at 6.52% own + NYM 5-stack — the trigger as written (35%+) would not have fired.

rules.text: Sharp-field ownership transform. For entry fees ≥ ~$100: transform projected ownership before any leverage math — structural chalk SP x1.5-1.7, model-consensus mid-priced stacks x0.5-0.6, obvious cheap value x2-4. Recompute chalk-live signals on transformed numbers. AMENDED v4 — applies ABOVE ~500 entries. Below that threshold #51 governs and the HITTER multiplier INVERTS. The ~1.0x ace-SP multiplier holds at both field sizes.
rules.rationale: 7/26: Miso 42.3→70.5. 7/27 confirmed the direction: Imai +8.4 while Burns -10.7 and Sproat -10.0.

rules.text: Full-tier SP2 candidacy. The SP2 set must include every gate-passing arm at every salary tier — never truncate to the premium tier. Price the bat-budget value of each $2K-$3K in SP savings.
rules.rationale: 7/26: top-3 all paired the ace with a $7,400-7,500 arm; Sheehan never a candidate.

rules.text: Small-field objective swap. Below ~1,000 entries: optimize for zero-dead-bat consistency plus a single spike (dk75/dk95-weighted), and VOID the 1-3-dead-bat tolerance of #26. AMENDED v4 — no longer advisory. Dead bats constrained by #49; the spike required by #52.
rules.rationale: 7/26 winner: 16-13-12-17-16-17-14-33, zero zeros, 437-entry field. 7/28 CONFIRMED BY CROSS-ENTRY: one lineup set entered into both a 334-entry WTA and a large-field GPP went 0/10 (needed top 3.6%) and 4/10 (needed ~top 20%). Same four lineups, same 10th-36th percentile band — one outcome priced by two curves.

rules.text: Stack-side gate validation. Every stack must be justified by the OPPOSING pitcher's gate failure, and the validator must assert the named pitcher's team ≠ the stack's team. SPLIT v4 — the validator team-identity assertion is RETAINED as a gate. The CLEAR/BLOCK gate verdict (no stack ships against an arm that PASSES the gate) is FOLDED INTO #50.
rules.rationale: 7/27: ATH stacked on Perkins' .500 vs RHH — Perkins is Oakland's own pitcher. ATH faced Tolle (.350/.290, PASS), scored 30 from five bats, 0 of top 100.

rules.text: Surviving-mechanism review. When a confirmed lineup kills the primary carve (handedness flip, scratch, order change), the secondary mechanism against that same arm must be re-scored before the team is dropped. A dead primary signal is a downgrade, never an automatic zero.
rules.rationale: 7/27: Pérez's .600 vs LHH died on a righty lineup; his NEGATIVE K-BB vs RHH survived and was discarded. NYM went 10.94x into the top 100. Also 7/26 (Murakami).

rules.text: Park factor is a weighting input, not a matchup substitute. Park and weather boosts modify allocation weight for a stack that already clears the gate test; they never justify a stack on their own. FOLDED INTO #50 — v4. Generalised from park inputs to all single-factor screens.
rules.rationale: 7/27: Sutter's +34% HR and 18.1% aggregate ownership carried the ATH stack past a gate-passing arm. Extends #3 to park inputs.

rules.text: Active delay ≠ forecast risk. A game in an ANNOUNCED delay at lock is capped at 3 bats in any single lineup and may not exceed one-third of portfolio stacks. #11's ~15% cap applies to forecast uncertainty only. Where lock time equals first pitch of an at-risk game, treat the game as unresolvable and size accordingly.
rules.rationale: 7/27: CLE@CIN in active delay at the 7:10 lock, 25-30% PPD estimate; PPD'd, zeroing five bats and ~45 pts.

rules.text: Dead-bat ceiling is a HARD BUILD CONSTRAINT below ~1,000 entries, not an objective term. Cap projected dead bats at ≤1 per lineup by construction; enforce the per-hitter floor at the dk25 level, not dk50 ≥ 4. Reject the lineup — do not down-weight it.
rules.rationale: 7/28: dead-bat count predicted finish monotonically across all 334 entries (0 dead → 149.6 mean; 4 dead → 95.7). Every top-12 lineup had ≤3; ours averaged 3.1. #44 named this and the build never enforced it.

rules.text: SINGLE-FACTOR SCREENS ARE WEIGHTS, NEVER GATES. The opposing-SP xSLG test RANKS stacks and arms; it never excludes one. Any team in the slate's top 5 by projected stack median or implied total enters the candidate set regardless of screen verdict. Absorbs #1, #31, #47 and the gate clause of #45.
rules.rationale: 7/28: blocked MIL (2nd, 107.0), LAD (4th, 92.0), SEA (5th, 81.0) while clearing STL (17th, 26.0). Winner ran SD5+SEA2; 2nd ran MIL4+LAD2. THIRD slate with this root — 6/30 (#1 deleted Cavalli/Wrobleski/Liberatore), 7/27 (#47), 7/28 (#45).

rules.text: Small-field ownership COMPRESSES toward the mean — invert the #42 hitter transform. Below ~500 entries at $100+ entry: hitter chalk x~0.5, sub-2% plays x~3-5, ace SP x~1.0. COROLLARY: leverage has minimal value in small fields — build the best lineup rather than buying differentiation from a crowd that is not there.
rules.rationale: 7/28: Romy Gonzalez 53.5%→3.6% (0.07x); Kwan 0.39x; Rocchio 0.42x; DeLauter 0.46x; JRam 0.48x; Williams 1.07x; Murakami 6.84x. Winner's cumulative ownership was 172 — the HIGHEST in the top 12.

rules.text: One 25+ ceiling bat per lineup is MANDATORY in small-field winner-take-all. Every lineup carries at least one hitter whose dk95 supports 25+, sized by ownership rather than by projection.
rules.rationale: 7/28: best hitter across ten lineups was 20.0. All five top finishers carried 23+. Field mean by spike: 20+ → 108.2, 25+ → 110.8, 30+ → 120.1.

rules.text: The discarded-signal log (#46) is upgraded to a HARD FORCE-REVIEW. Any confirmed, sub-2%-owned bat with xSLG ≥ .45 that a standing rule blocks must be adjudicated IN WRITING before the build ships. No build ships with an unadjudicated blocked signal.
rules.rationale: 7/28: the rescan surfaced Canzone (0.8% own, .47 xSLG, scored 30.00) plus Ohtani/Tucker/Freeman; #45 killed all of them silently. FOURTH consecutive slate of a correct pre-slate signal dying in the confirmed-lineup phase (7/26 Murakami, 7/27 Pérez, 7/28 Canzone).

governance.rules_to_slates_ratio: 48 active / ~16 studied slates, flagged as a live risk in v4 Section 11
governance.retire_policy: A rule that has misfired and been amended twice is RETIRED, not amended a third time.
governance.no_new_contradicting_rule: No new rule may be adopted in the same post-mortem cycle as a rule it contradicts. Before adopting, check the new rule against every rule added in the previous three post-mortems.
consolidation_candidates_next_review: #12/#37/#38 all govern chalk-SP treatment and could collapse into one classification rule with three branches
#29/#33 both cap concentration in different domains
open_items: Ownership calibration curve: #51's multipliers rest on two slates; log projected-vs-actual every slate.
Entry-count question: whether small-field WTA should use max entries at all — ten lineups at 3.1 mean dead bats generated no equity on 7/28.
